subject: Geopolitics
title: The Gulf Wars and Oil
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Gulf Wars and Oil.

hook.text: Saddam Hussein invaded Kuwait in 1990 for its oil. The US responded with 500,000 troops in weeks.

buildup.text: Kuwait held 10% of global oil reserves. Letting one dictator control it would shift the power balance.

discovery.text: The Gulf Wars showed that oil isn't just economic — it's a security issue that justifies massive intervention.

twist.text: The 2003 Iraq War was sold as WMD disarmament. Critics called it an oil grab. The truth lies in between.

climax.text: Both wars reshaped the Middle East. Trillions were spent. The region is still unstable decades later.

punchline.text: Oil draws armies the way honey draws flies.

quiz.question: Why did the US respond so quickly to Iraq's invasion of Kuwait?
options: Kuwait held 10% of global oil reserves
Iraq threatened to use nuclear weapons
